Subject: Dedicated capacity SLA clarifications for RL POC

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the call last week — the Rainwood POC is progressing and the engineering team is starting to hit steady-state traffic. We wanted to surface a couple of operational questions before we scale to the reserved pool:

- We observed intermittent tail latency spikes during concurrent batch windows (attached snapshot). Can you clarify how reserved GPU queueing behaves when an inbound burst collides with a scheduled nightly batch?
- What explicit throughput guarantees do you provide per reserved GPU (tokens/sec or inferences/sec) for RL-optimized models? We need numbers for our SRE runbook and procurement.
- Is there a documented ops playbook (escalation/runbook) that covers fallback to model variants, burst tokens, and preemption windows? Procurement expects this for the contract.

I'm attaching a short SLO snapshot we pulled from our staging run. Can we get a short ops playbook and some concrete throughput numbers? Happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Director of ML Ops
Rainwood Labs

Hi Maya — thanks for sending this over (and for the snapshot). Putting Lauren and Ben on the thread to make sure ops and commercial are aligned.

Quick answers up front:
- Reserved GPUs are scheduled into a tenant-specific pool with a fairness window (configurable). During scheduled nightly batches we do not preempt reserved capacity for cross-tenant bursts, but we do support configurable burst tokens and short-term burst reservations for predictable windows.
- I’m attaching our standard SLA summary with baseline throughput guidance; we can produce more precise numbers once we know the model variant and sequence-length distribution.

Lauren/B — can you share the ops playbook draft and proposed throughput baseline for a g5-like reserved instance running our RL-optimized 30B variant?

If it helps, lets book a 30-min ops call tomorrow. I’ve pasted a draft playbook link below as well.

Cheers,

> Thanks again for the call last week — the Rainwood POC is progressing ...

Thanks for the details, Maya — good questions. High-level operational summary here; I attached a short playbook draft (ops_playbook_draft.md) as requested.

1) Queueing and fairness windows
- Reserved GPUs are insulated from best-effort pools via a tenant reservation that owns N GPUs. Within the reservation we implement a moving fairness window (default 60s) to avoid starvation across concurrent tenants sharing a pool. This is configurable per-contract.

2) Batch jobs and scheduled windows
- By default, scheduled batch windows are treated as resident tenant load and do not trigger eviction of reserved capacity. If you want a carveout to run heavy nightly batches without affecting latency for your low-latency endpoints, we can configure an explicit "batch carveout" window and apply burst tokens to the reserved pool.

3) Throughput baselines
- For the RL-optimized 30B variant on an rtx-like reserved GPU, baseline sustained throughput we observe is ~1.2M tokens / GPU / hour for mixed prompt lengths (seq 512 avg). Tail latency (95th) < 250 ms for single-stream interactive traffic under nominal load; under sustained high-concurrency batch windows, 95th can shift to ~800–1200 ms unless carveouts or burst tokens are applied. We can produce per-model, per-seq-length matrices.

4) Fallbacks and model variants
- Playbook includes automatic fallback to a quantized variant if queueing depth exceeds threshold and an emergency canary routing policy to a smaller model. That behavior is toggled per-route.

Next steps: Ben, can you propose contract language for a reserve + burst token addendum that includes a scheduled batch carveout and an ops-runbook delivery milestone?

Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager, Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: ops_playbook_draft.md

Thanks Lauren — that level of detail helps. A few follow-ups from procurement & SRE:

- Procurement will want explicit numbers in the contract: minimum sustained throughput per reserved GPU (tokens/hr or rps) and a defined headroom for scheduled batch carveouts (we propose 2x baseline for 2 hours nightly).
- SRE is worried about tail latency in multi-tenant runs; would you commit to a 95th percentile latency SLO for interactive endpoints when batch carveout is configured? If so, what's the crediting model if it's missed?
- We’ve attached a short CSV showing our nightly batch footprint (rainwood_batch_hist.csv). Can you propose a test plan (load test) that will validate the carveout and burst tokens before we sign?

Procurement also asked for an ops-runbook delivery milestone tied to the first invoice.

Can Ben outline the commercial addendum and the acceptance test plan? Otherwise we may need to move to a limited pilot until the carveout behavior is contractually explicit.

Best,
Maya
Attachment: rainwood_batch_hist.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@rainwoodlabs.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T15:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA clarification & ops playbook request - Rainwood Labs POC

Hi Maya — appreciate the clarity and the batch data. Proposed commercial and test approach below.

1) Commercial addendum (summary)
- Reserved pool: N GPUs (specified in SOW).
- Baseline throughput: guaranteed 1.1M tokens per GPU per hour (this is a contract baseline; we will publish detailed per-model matrices in the SOW appendix).
- Scheduled batch carveout: up to 2x baseline for a configurable 2-hour nightly window (Carveout Window). Carveout must be specified in calendar in the SOW.
- Latency SLO for interactive endpoints (when carveout configured): 95th < 350 ms measured by route-level telemetry. Credit model: pro-rated credit for missed SLO based on percent degradation (standard SLA credit table applies).

2) Ops/test plan (acceptance criteria)
- Pre-deployment load test: Redwood will run a joint validation run against your staging traffic patterns (we will use the supplied CSV). Success criteria: sustained baseline throughput within ±10% for 1 hour and 95th latency target met for interactive routes under carveout conditions.
- Post-provisioning: ops-runbook (deliverable) within 10 business days of first invoice; milestone payment tied to signed SOW.

3) Next steps
- I'll open a short JIRA (RL-POC-73) to track the acceptance tests and ops-runbook delivery.
- If this sounds good we can issue a concise addendum (DocuSign link below) that lists baseline numbers, carveout windows, and ops-runbook milestone.

If you want to tighten the baseline numbers we can run a 2-hour profiling session (we'll need model binary and representative prompts). Happy to coordinate times.

Ben Carter
Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference
